course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Polynomial and Rational Functions
unit.description: See how outputs change with inputs, then use rates of change, zeros, end behavior, asymptotes, and holes to describe polynomial and rational functions and build models from them.

firstTopic.title: Change in Tandem
firstTopic.summary: How inputs and outputs vary together: functions, increasing and decreasing behavior, concavity, and zeros.

topics.title: Change in Tandem
topics.summary: How inputs and outputs vary together: functions, increasing and decreasing behavior, concavity, and zeros.

topics.title: Rates of Change
topics.summary: Average rates of change over intervals, estimating the rate at a point, and what the sign of a rate tells you.

topics.title: Rates of Change in Linear and Quadratic Functions
topics.summary: How average rates behave for linear and quadratic functions, secant slopes, and reading concavity from changing rates.

topics.title: Polynomial Functions and Rates of Change
topics.summary: Polynomial vocabulary, local and global extrema, how zeros and turning points relate, and inflection points.

topics.title: Polynomial Functions and Complex Zeros
topics.summary: Zeros and factors, multiplicity, conjugate pairs of non-real zeros, finding degree from differences, and even and odd symmetry.

topics.title: Polynomial Functions and End Behavior
topics.summary: Limit notation, why the leading term controls the far left and far right of the graph, and the four end-behavior cases.

topics.title: Rational Functions and End Behavior
topics.summary: What a rational function is, and how comparing leading terms gives horizontal and slant asymptotes.

topics.title: Rational Functions and Zeros
topics.summary: Finding the zeros of a rational function and using signs to decide where it is positive or negative.

topics.title: Rational Functions and Vertical Asymptotes
topics.summary: Where the denominator is zero but the numerator is not, and how one-sided limits describe the graph nearby.

topics.title: Rational Functions and Holes
topics.summary: When a factor cancels, the graph has a hole instead of an asymptote, and how to find its coordinates.

topics.title: Equivalent Representations of Polynomial and Rational Expressions
topics.summary: Rewriting expressions by factoring, expanding, dividing, and using the binomial theorem, and choosing the form that shows what you need.

topics.title: Transformations of Functions
topics.summary: How shifts, dilations, and reflections change a function's graph, its points, its domain and range, and its asymptotes.

topics.title: Function Model Selection and Assumption Articulation
topics.summary: Choosing a type of function to model a situation, using successive differences, and stating the assumptions and restrictions that come with a model.

topics.title: Function Model Construction and Application
topics.summary: Building a function model from conditions, a parent function, or technology, and interpreting the model in context.
